title: JNI Boundaries, References, Threads, and Exceptions Check

questions.prompt: Which approach best applies jni boundaries, references, threads, and exceptions?
options: Minimise crossings and make thread, reference, buffer, exception, handle, and callback ownership explicit and tested.
questions.answer: Minimise crossings and make thread, reference, buffer, exception, handle, and callback ownership explicit and tested.
questions.explanation: The correct response preserves authority, compatibility, exact artifact evidence, adverse-path behavior, and operational ownership.

questions.prompt: A JNI local reference can be stored and safely used from any native thread until the process exits.
questions.explanation: Caching JNIEnv in a global and using it from worker threads violates its thread affinity and can corrupt runtime interaction.

questions.prompt: What must a native-created thread do before using JNI?
questions.answer: Attach to the JavaVM to obtain its own JNIEnv, then detach before the thread terminates.
questions.explanation: The answer identifies the contract or mechanism that remains valid beyond one implementation demonstration.
